transcript.text: dryer drum wont turn but i can here it running, hotpiont. clothes just sit there

This connects the motor to the drum; if it's broken, the motor runs freely while the clothes just sit there. 1. Unplug the dryer and make sure the drum is empty.
2. Turn the drum slowly by hand. What does it feel like?
• If it spins round very easily with no resistance at all (like a wheel on bearings), the belt is likely broken or off its pulley.
• If it feels stiff, hard to turn, or grinds, there may be an obstruction or worn rollers.
• If it turns normally but the motor still won't drive it when plugged in, we'll look at the next possibility (the motor capacitor). Please let me know exactly how the drum feels when you turn it by hand.
ok unplugged it and turned the drum by hand and it spins really easy, almost no resistance at all

The motor is doing its job, but there's nothing left to transfer that power to the drum. 1. Unplug the dryer and open the door.
2. Look inside at the back of the drum (you may need a torch). You should see a rubber belt wrapped around the outer edge of the drum and connected to a motor pulley at the bottom or side.
3. Check if the belt is still there as a complete loop, or if it has snapped/is hanging loose/off the pulley. If you can't easily see inside without removing panels (which requires an engineer for safety), just let me know that you've checked and couldn't see it clearly. If you can see it and it's broken or off, that is your fault - the belt needs replacing.
ok had a look with a torch thru the filter slot and under the drum and i can see a black rubbery strip lying at the bottom. i have a screwdriver set if i need to take the back panel off

[Heading: Likely cause: drive belt]
That suggests it: the belt has snapped or slipped off its pulley. To get you the right replacement part, I need the model number. It’s usually on a sticker inside the door frame (look around the rubber seal) or sometimes on the back of the machine. Could you read that out to me?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
the sticker is a bit worn so i can only read the start of it, it says TVHM8 and then cant make out the rest. 6 yrs old hotpoint if that helps

[Heading: Likely cause: drive belt]
That suggests it: the black rubbery strip you saw is the drive belt. I won't give you a specific part number to avoid ordering the wrong item. However, this is a very standard repair on Hotpoint dryers. 1. Order the part yourself: Search for "Hotpoint TVHM8 drive belt" or visit the manufacturer's official spare parts site and enter whatever full model number you can find (often on the back of the machine or inside the door frame). The part is usually inexpensive.
2. Call an engineer: If you prefer not to dismantle the machine, a local engineer will replace this quickly. If you choose to do it yourself: ensure the dryer is unplugged. You will likely need to remove the top panel and/or the front or rear panel (depending on your specific model layout) to access the drum and motor pulley. Once accessible, fit the new belt around the drum, then loop it over the motor pulley and the tensioner/idler wheel. Reassemble and test. If you are unsure about accessing the internals safely, please call an engineer.
